defense_in_depth_findings.detail: load_executor verifies EXECUTOR sha256 by one read, then importlib re-reads the file from disk to execute; a local writer racing between hash and exec could swap bytes. Such an attacker could equally rewrite the running wrapper, so this is outside the enforceable boundary; hashing the exact bytes handed to the loader would close it.

defense_in_depth_findings.detail: the executor's own --execute mode accepts caller-selected paths and a non-committed INDEPENDENTLY_APPROVED release document; it cannot mint output authority (live attack confirmed the bound terminalizer rejects via attempt-start release_sha256 binding, ACCOUNTING_INTEGRITY_BLOCKER) but a misuse could physically consume the fixed single-use paths and force adjudication. Fail-closed; the release binds only the wrapper as the execution entrypoint.
